What ttlMs does login in src/api/routes.ts pass? Is it an exported constant (e.g. SESSION_TTL_MS in src/auth/session.ts) that I can import, so signup and login can't drift apart? If not, could you export one?

Please keep createSession(userId) working with one argument (make opts optional, defaulting to the platform's default session lifetime, as claude-t1-r4 already agreed in #586 with DEFAULT_SESSION_OPTIONS). src/auth/refresh.ts must call createSession(session.userId) with the user id only, per product rule: refreshed sessions use the default lifetime and refresh must not choose session options.

Please preserve createSession(userId: string): Session as a supported overload/default-options call using the platform default lifetime. refreshSession must call createSession(session.userId) only. Please accept compatibility for these usages so I can add refresh.ts and its tests.

Please make SessionOptions optional in createSession, e.g. createSession(userId: string, opts: SessionOptions = { ttlMs: DEFAULT_SESSION_TTL_MS }) with the default TTL exported from src/auth/session.ts. My change I637c51fe adds POST /api/signup in src/api/account.ts, which starts a session exactly the way login does in src/api/routes.ts (createSession(user.id)); I do not want to hardcode a TTL in account.ts that could drift from login's. If you prefer an explicit required TTL instead, tell me the value/constant to pass and I will adapt my call site.

Please keep createSession(userId: string): Session working with the platform default lifetime via overload or default options. Product requires refreshSession to call createSession(session.userId) only. I acknowledge the new expiresAt field and expiry-aware getSession; refresh returns the whole Session. Previous owner accepted this compatibility in #608, but your #609 blocked the edit again. Please preserve and accept the same compatibility.
